chunks.heading: ADR-0007: adopt Helix Mesh for east-west traffic
chunks.text:
ADR-0007: adopt Helix Mesh for east-west traffic

# ADR-0007: adopt Helix Mesh for east-west traffic

> **Superseded by [ADR-0019](adr-0019-calder-gateway.md) (2026-02-11).** Helix
> Mesh is being removed from all tiers. Do not start new work against it. This
> record stays because three runbooks and two postmortems still reference it,
> and deleting it would leave those citations dangling.

- **Status:** superseded
- **Date:** 2024-06-03
- **Deciders:** Platform Networking, Calder Group

chunks.heading: Context
chunks.text:
Context

## Context

Calder Group runs roughly 2 400 services across four regions. Before this
decision, east-west traffic used per-service client libraries: each team
shipped its own retry policy, its own timeout, and its own idea of what a
circuit breaker was. A single slow dependency produced four different
behaviours depending on which team's library was calling it.

The 2024 Q1 review counted eleven distinct retry implementations in the
checkout path alone. Two of them retried non-idempotent writes.

chunks.heading: Decision
chunks.text:
Decision

## Decision

Adopt **Helix Mesh** as the mandatory sidecar for all east-west traffic.

1. Every service gets a sidecar injected at admission time. There is no opt-out
   short of a platform exception, and exceptions expire after 90 days.
2. Retry, timeout and circuit-breaking policy moves into mesh configuration and
   out of application code.
3. mTLS between all services, with certificates rotated every 24 hours.
4. Client libraries are frozen: bug fixes only, no new policy features.

chunks.heading: Consequences
chunks.text:
Consequences

## Consequences

- **Policy becomes reviewable.** A retry budget is a diff in a config repo
  rather than a constant compiled into eleven binaries.
- **A per-request latency cost of 1.2–1.8 ms** at p50, measured on the
  checkout path. Accepted deliberately: the review judged consistency worth
  more than a millisecond.
- **The sidecar becomes a shared failure domain.** A bad mesh rollout can take
  down every service at once, which is a class of outage the per-library world
  did not have. The rollback runbook is
  [the legacy mesh rollback](runbook-mesh-rollback-legacy.md).
- **Memory overhead of ~180 MB per pod.** At 2 400 services this is real money
  and it is the number that eventually forced ADR-0019.

chunks.heading: Alternatives considered
chunks.text:
Alternatives considered

## Alternatives considered

- **A shared client library, mandated.** Rejected: mandating a library means
  mandating a language, and Calder runs Go, Java, Python and Rust in
  production.
- **API gateway only, no service-to-service policy.** Rejected: it addresses
  north-south traffic and leaves the eleven retry implementations untouched.
- **Do nothing and write a style guide.** Rejected on evidence — the 2023 style
  guide said exactly what the eleven implementations should have done.

chunks.heading: Operational notes
chunks.text:
Operational notes

## Operational notes

Mesh configuration lives in `calder/mesh-policy`. A policy change is a pull
request; the platform team reviews anything that touches a retry budget or a
timeout, because those two are what turn a slow dependency into an outage.

Rollout is per-tier, following [the deployment tiers](reference-deployment-tiers.md):
tier 3 first, then tier 2, then tier 1, with a 48-hour soak between each.

The on-call rotation for the mesh itself is separate from the service rotation
— see [the on-call rota](guide-oncall-rota.md).

title: "ADR-0019: replace Helix Mesh with Calder Gateway"
tags: [architecture, networking, current]

chunks.heading: ADR-0019: replace Helix Mesh with Calder Gateway
chunks.text:
ADR-0019: replace Helix Mesh with Calder Gateway

# ADR-0019: replace Helix Mesh with Calder Gateway

> **Supersedes [ADR-0007](adr-0007-helix-mesh.md).** Helix Mesh is removed tier
> by tier through 2026. **This is the current decision for east-west traffic.**

- **Status:** accepted
- **Date:** 2026-02-11
- **Deciders:** Platform Networking, Calder Group, with SRE sign-off

chunks.heading: Context
chunks.text:
Context

## Context

[ADR-0007](adr-0007-helix-mesh.md) achieved what it set out to: retry policy is
reviewable, mTLS is universal, and the eleven retry implementations are gone.
It also cost more than anyone modelled.

Three numbers drove the reversal:

| | 2024 estimate | 2026 measured |
|---|---|---|
| memory per pod | 180 MB | **310 MB** |
| p50 added latency | 1.2–1.8 ms | **2.9 ms** |
| fleet cost of the sidecar | not modelled | **~14 % of compute spend** |

The memory figure is the decisive one. At 2 400 services and a median of six
replicas, the sidecar fleet is larger than the application fleet it serves.

chunks.heading: Decision
chunks.text:
Decision

## Decision

Replace the sidecar mesh with **Calder Gateway**, a shared per-node proxy.

1. **One proxy per node, not one per pod.** Policy is unchanged in meaning;
   only its placement moves.
2. **Retry, timeout and circuit-breaking configuration is carried forward
   verbatim.** The migration must not be a policy change and a placement change
   at the same time — that is how a migration becomes an incident nobody can
   attribute.
3. **mTLS terminates at the node proxy.** This is a real reduction in isolation
   and it is accepted with a compensating control: node-level network policy is
   now mandatory rather than advisory.
4. **Tier 3 first, then tier 2, then tier 1**, per
   [the deployment tiers](reference-deployment-tiers.md), with a 14-day soak
   between tiers rather than 48 hours. The longer soak is a direct consequence
   of the [checkout outage postmortem](postmortem-checkout-outage.md).

chunks.heading: Consequences
chunks.text:
Consequences

## Consequences

- **Expected saving of roughly 11 % of compute spend**, and a p50 latency
  reduction of about 2 ms on the checkout path.
- **Blast radius moves from the pod to the node.** A bad proxy config now takes
  out every workload on that node. The mitigation is the tiered rollout and the
  new soak period, not a claim that it cannot happen.
- **The rollback procedure changed** and is
  [the gateway rollback runbook](runbook-gateway-rollback.md). The old
  [legacy mesh rollback](runbook-mesh-rollback-legacy.md) still applies to any
  tier that has not migrated, which through 2026 is most of tier 1.
- **Two rollback runbooks exist simultaneously**, and that is the single most
  dangerous fact about this migration. On-call must check which one applies
  before touching anything.

chunks.heading: Alternatives considered
chunks.text:
Alternatives considered

## Alternatives considered

- **Tune the sidecar.** Attempted for two quarters. Memory fell from 310 MB to
  270 MB and stopped; the floor is the proxy's own connection state.
- **Return to client libraries.** Rejected for the same reason ADR-0007
  rejected them: four languages.
- **eBPF-based policy with no proxy at all.** Genuinely attractive and rejected
  on maturity, not on merit. Reopen if the kernel floor across the fleet
  reaches 6.4 and the policy surface covers retry budgets.

chunks.heading: Guide: onboarding to the Calder platform
chunks.text:
Guide: onboarding to the Calder platform

# Guide: onboarding to the Calder platform

For an engineer shipping their first service. Expect half a day.

## Before you start

You need: cluster access (`calderctl --context` resolves), membership of your
team's group, and a service name approved in `calder/service-registry`. Names
are permanent — they appear in metrics, alerts and billing exports — so the
registry review is slower than it looks like it should be.

chunks.heading: 1. Register the service and pick a tier
chunks.text:
1. Register the service and pick a tier

## 1. Register the service and pick a tier

Every service belongs to exactly one tier, and **a service without a tier does
not deploy** — the admission controller rejects it. Read
[the deployment tiers](reference-deployment-tiers.md) before you choose.

Most first services are **tier 3**. Choosing tier 1 because it sounds important
buys you two reviewers, a 14-day soak and a 24/7 page rotation, and you will
regret all three.

chunks.heading: 2. State your data classification
chunks.text:
2. State your data classification

## 2. State your data classification

In the same registry entry. If you do not state it, the platform treats your
service as holding the most sensitive class — see
[the data retention policy](policy-data-retention.md). This is not a formality:
it decides your encryption requirements and your backup window.

chunks.heading: 3. Deploy to tier 3
chunks.text:
3. Deploy to tier 3

## 3. Deploy to tier 3

```
calderctl deploy <service> --tier 3 --version 0.1.0 --dry-run
calderctl deploy <service> --tier 3 --version 0.1.0
```

Full flag reference: [the calderctl CLI](reference-calderctl.md).

chunks.heading: 4. Understand what the platform does for you
chunks.text:
4. Understand what the platform does for you

## 4. Understand what the platform does for you

- **Traffic policy is not yours.** Retry, timeout and circuit-breaking live in
  platform config, not your code. Do not add a retry loop; you will be retrying
  a request the proxy is already retrying, and the multiplication is how a slow
  dependency becomes an outage.
- **mTLS is automatic.** You do not manage certificates.
- **Which proxy you get depends on your tier's migration state** —
  [Calder Gateway](adr-0019-calder-gateway.md) if migrated, Helix Mesh if not.
  As a service owner this should be invisible. It stops being invisible during
  an incident, which is why the two rollback runbooks exist separately.

chunks.heading: 5. Wire up alerting
chunks.text:
5. Wire up alerting

## 5. Wire up alerting

Route pages according to your tier. **A tier 3 service must not page anyone.**
If your alert pages at 03:00 and your service is tier 3, that is a routing bug.
See [the on-call rota](guide-oncall-rota.md).

chunks.heading: 6. Join the rotation
chunks.text:
6. Join the rotation

## 6. Join the rotation

Once you are in tier 2 or 1 you join your team's service on-call. Read the
rota guide first, particularly the part about which of the three rotations to
page. Paging platform networking for your own service's bug is the most common
first-month mistake.

chunks.heading: Common first-month mistakes
chunks.text:
Common first-month mistakes

## Common first-month mistakes

| mistake | what happens |
|---|---|
| Adding an application-level retry | double retries; a slow dependency becomes an outage |
| Choosing tier 1 for a new service | 14-day soak on every change |
| Leaving data class unstated | treated as C3; HSM requirements you do not need |
| Paging platform for your own bug | ten minutes lost while they ask what your service does |
| Reading the wrong rollback runbook | see [the checkout outage](postmortem-checkout-outage.md) |

title: "Guide: the on-call rota"
tags: [operations, oncall, guide]
---

chunks.heading: Guide: the on-call rota
chunks.text:
Guide: the on-call rota

# Guide: the on-call rota

Calder Group runs **three independent rotations**. Confusing them is the most
common cause of a page going to someone who cannot act on it.

| rotation | covers | handover |
|---|---|---|
| **service on-call** | one team's own services | Monday 10:00 local |
| **platform networking** | Calder Gateway, Helix Mesh, node proxy config | Monday 10:00 UTC |
| **incident lead** | coordination during a SEV1/SEV2 | Wednesday 14:00 UTC |

chunks.heading: Who to page, and when
chunks.text:
Who to page, and when

## Who to page, and when

- **Your own service is unhealthy** → your team's service on-call. Do not page
  platform first; platform will ask you what your service is doing and you will
  have lost ten minutes.
- **Traffic between services is failing, across teams** → platform networking.
  This is the rotation the rollback runbooks name
  ([gateway](runbook-gateway-rollback.md),
  [legacy mesh](runbook-mesh-rollback-legacy.md)).
- **More than one team is affected, or the revenue path is down** → incident
  lead, *in addition* to the above. The incident lead does not fix things; they
  hold the timeline and decide when to declare and when to close.

chunks.heading: Page policy by tier
chunks.text:
Page policy by tier

## Page policy by tier

Page behaviour follows [the deployment tiers](reference-deployment-tiers.md):
tier 1 pages 24/7, tier 2 pages in business hours, tier 3 never pages.

A tier 3 alert that pages someone at 03:00 is a routing misconfiguration. Fix
the routing; do not normalise the page.

chunks.heading: Handover
chunks.text:
Handover

## Handover

Handover is a written note in `#platform-oncall`, not a verbal one. It names:

1. anything currently degraded,
2. any freeze in effect (`calderctl gateway status --by-tier` shows these),
3. any rollout mid-flight and which tier it is on,
4. anything you escalated that has not resolved.

**A handover that says "all quiet" when a rollout is mid-flight is the specific
failure this list exists to prevent.** A rollout is not quiet; it is a thing
that might page the next person.

chunks.heading: Escalation
chunks.text:
Escalation

## Escalation

If you are the on-call and you do not know what to do, escalate. The median
time-to-escalate during the
[checkout outage](postmortem-checkout-outage.md) was 31 minutes, and 18 of
those minutes were a second rollback attempt the runbook explicitly says not to
make. **Escalating early has never made an incident worse here.**

chunks.heading: Compensation and limits
chunks.text:
Compensation and limits

## Compensation and limits

- No engineer is on call more than one week in four.
- A page between 22:00 and 07:00 local buys the following morning off, and this
  is not discretionary.
- Two consecutive nights paged means the rotation is handed over. Tell the
  incident lead; they will find cover.

title: "Policy: data retention and classification"
tags: [policy, compliance, data]
---

chunks.heading: Policy: data retention and classification
chunks.text:
Policy: data retention and classification

# Policy: data retention and classification

**Binding on every Calder Group service.** A service that cannot state its data
classification is treated as holding the most sensitive class until it can.

chunks.heading: Classes
chunks.text:
Classes

## Classes

| class | examples | retention | encryption at rest |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C0 public** | published docs, marketing | indefinite | not required |
| **C1 internal** | dashboards, build logs, tickets | 400 days | required |
| **C2 personal** | account records, addresses, order history | 7 years | required, per-tenant key |
| **C3 payment** | card tokens, settlement records | 7 years | required, per-tenant key, HSM |

**Raw card numbers are C3 and are never stored.** Tokens are stored; the number
that produced them is not, anywhere, including in logs, traces and crash dumps.

chunks.heading: Retention is a maximum, not a target
chunks.text:
Retention is a maximum, not a target

## Retention is a maximum, not a target

A service holding C2 data for 7 years must be able to say *why*. The default
for anything without a stated legal or contractual reason is **90 days**, and
the compliance review asks for the reason rather than for the duration.

chunks.heading: Logs are data
chunks.text:
Logs are data

## Logs are data

The most common finding in the 2025 audit was C2 data in C1 log stores — an
address in an error message, an email in a stack trace. Log lines inherit the
classification of the most sensitive field they contain.

**A log store cannot be reclassified downward by deleting the offending
lines**, because backups already hold them. The remedy is to stop emitting and
to expire the backup window.

chunks.heading: Deletion requests
chunks.text:
Deletion requests

## Deletion requests

A verified deletion request must complete within 30 days across:

1. primary stores,
2. read replicas and caches,
3. search indexes,
4. analytics warehouses,
5. backups — by expiry rather than by surgical deletion, which is why the
   backup window is 35 days and not longer.

Point 5 is the one teams miss. **A 90-day backup window means a 90-day deletion
SLA**, and that is not the SLA.

chunks.heading: Tiers and classification are independent
chunks.text:
Tiers and classification are independent

## Tiers and classification are independent

Data class is not deployment tier. See
[the deployment tiers](reference-deployment-tiers.md): a tier 3 internal
dashboard routinely holds C2 data, and its tier says nothing about how that
data must be handled. Confusing the two is how a low-tier internal tool ends up
outside the audit scope.

chunks.heading: Exceptions
chunks.text:
Exceptions

## Exceptions

Exceptions are granted by the data protection lead, expire in 180 days, and are
recorded in `calder/compliance-exceptions`. **An expired exception is a
violation**, not a renewal request; the service must be compliant on the expiry
date or it is turned off.

title: "Postmortem: checkout unavailable for 47 minutes (2026-01-19)"
tags: [incident, postmortem, checkout]
---

chunks.heading: Postmortem: checkout unavailable for 47 minutes
chunks.text:
Postmortem: checkout unavailable for 47 minutes

# Postmortem: checkout unavailable for 47 minutes

- **Date:** 2026-01-19 · **Duration:** 47 minutes · **Severity:** SEV1
- **Impact:** checkout returned 503 for an estimated 31 % of sessions in
  eu-west and us-east. No data loss. No incorrect charges.

chunks.heading: Summary
chunks.text:
Summary

## Summary

A routine Helix Mesh sidecar rollback on tier 1 silently skipped 340 pods whose
sidecar injection failed. Those pods came back with **no sidecar at all**, so
they had no mTLS identity, and every call they made to the payments service was
rejected at the receiving end. Checkout depends on payments, so checkout failed.

The rollback reported success. Aggregate health looked fine because 340 pods
out of roughly 9 000 is under 4 %, and the aggregate dashboard's alert
threshold is 5 %.

chunks.heading: Timeline
chunks.text:
Timeline

## Timeline

| time (UTC) | event |
|---|---|
| 14:02 | Mesh release 4.19.2 begins tier 1 rollout |
| 14:31 | Error rate on payments crosses 2 %; on-call paged |
| 14:38 | On-call begins the legacy mesh rollback, tier 1 |
| 14:44 | Rollback reports success. Error rate does not recover |
| 14:51 | Second rollback attempted. No change |
| 15:09 | Engineer notices pods with a single container where two are expected |
| 15:18 | 340 pods identified and restarted by hand |
| 15:25 | Error rate recovers |
| 15:38 | Incident closed after a 5-minute clean window |

chunks.heading: What went wrong
chunks.text:
What went wrong

## What went wrong

**1. Failed sidecar injection is silent.** The rollback tooling skips a pod it
cannot inject and does not count it as a failure. This is named as a known gap
in [the legacy mesh rollback](runbook-mesh-rollback-legacy.md), and it had been
named there for eleven months.

**2. The aggregate dashboard hid it.** 340 of 9 000 is 3.8 %, under the 5 %
alert threshold. Verification was done in aggregate rather than per service —
the runbook says per service, and the on-call engineer used the aggregate view
because it is the default panel.

**3. The second rollback attempt cost 18 minutes.** The runbook says escalate
rather than retry. It was retried.

chunks.heading: What did not go wrong
chunks.text:
What did not go wrong

## What did not go wrong

- The rollback procedure itself is correct. Following it exactly would have
  caught this at step 4.
- mTLS rejecting unauthenticated callers is the system working. A checkout that
  succeeded without an identity would have been a far worse outcome.

chunks.heading: Actions
chunks.text:
Actions

## Actions

| action | owner | status |
|---|---|---|
| Injection failure becomes a hard error, not a skip | Platform Networking | done 2026-02-02 |
| Per-service verification becomes the default dashboard panel | SRE | done 2026-01-27 |
| **Soak period between tiers raised from 48 hours to 14 days** | Platform Networking | done, recorded in [ADR-0019](adr-0019-calder-gateway.md) |
| Dry-run mode for both rollback runbooks | Platform Networking | **not started** |

chunks.heading: The lesson worth carrying
chunks.text:
The lesson worth carrying

## The lesson worth carrying

**A known gap that has been written down for eleven months is not mitigated.**
The failure mode in this incident was documented, in the runbook the on-call
engineer had open, in a section titled "Known gaps". Writing a hazard down does
not remove it; the action item is what removes it, and there was none.

title: "Reference: the calderctl CLI"
tags: [reference, tooling, platform]
---

chunks.heading: Reference: the `calderctl` CLI
chunks.text:
Reference: the `calderctl` CLI

# Reference: the `calderctl` CLI

The platform CLI. Everything below is read-only unless marked **writes**.

## Global flags

| flag | effect |
|---|---|
| `--tier <n>` | scope to one deployment tier. **Required by every write command** — there is no fleet-wide write, deliberately |
| `--json` | machine-readable output |
| `--dry-run` | supported by `deploy` and `quota`. **Not** by `gateway rollback` or `mesh rollback`, which is a known gap |
| `--context <cluster>` | defaults to the cluster in `~/.calder/config` |

chunks.heading: `calderctl gateway`
chunks.text:
`calderctl gateway`

## `calderctl gateway`

```
calderctl gateway status --by-tier          # which release each tier runs
calderctl gateway freeze --tier <n>         # writes: halt an in-flight rollout
calderctl gateway unfreeze --tier <n>       # writes
calderctl gateway rollback --tier <n> --to <release> --max-surge 1   # writes
calderctl gateway verify --tier <n> --per-node
```

`--max-surge 1` is mandatory on gateway rollback. The proxy is per node, so
surging more than one node removes capacity from every workload on those nodes
at once. The full procedure is
[the gateway rollback runbook](runbook-gateway-rollback.md).

chunks.heading: `calderctl mesh` — legacy
chunks.text:
`calderctl mesh` — legacy

## `calderctl mesh` — legacy

```
calderctl mesh status --by-tier
calderctl mesh freeze --tier <n>            # writes
calderctl mesh rollback --tier <n> --to <release> --max-surge 25%   # writes
calderctl mesh verify --tier <n> --per-service
```

Applies only to tiers still on Helix Mesh ([ADR-0007](adr-0007-helix-mesh.md),
superseded by [ADR-0019](adr-0019-calder-gateway.md)). Procedure:
[the legacy mesh rollback](runbook-mesh-rollback-legacy.md).

**The two rollback commands take different `--max-surge` values and this is the
most dangerous pair of flags in the tool.** Copying a gateway command onto a
mesh tier surges 1 pod at a time across thousands and takes hours; copying a
mesh command onto a gateway tier surges a quarter of the nodes and removes a
quarter of the fleet.

chunks.heading: `calderctl deploy`
chunks.text:
`calderctl deploy`

## `calderctl deploy`

```
calderctl deploy <service> --tier <n> --version <v>   # writes
calderctl deploy <service> --tier <n> --version <v> --dry-run
calderctl deploy status <service>
```

Refuses a service with no tier in `calder/service-registry`. Refuses a tier 1
deploy without two reviewers, one from SRE, per
[the deployment tiers](reference-deployment-tiers.md).

chunks.heading: `calderctl quota`
chunks.text:
`calderctl quota`

## `calderctl quota`

```
calderctl quota show <service>
calderctl quota set <service> --cpu <n> --memory <n>  # writes, platform team only
```

chunks.heading: `calderctl data`
chunks.text:
`calderctl data`

## `calderctl data`

```
calderctl data classify <service>       # the stated class, from the registry
calderctl data expiry <service>         # retention window per store
```

Both read from `calder/service-registry`. A service whose class is unstated
reports `C3` — the most sensitive — per
[the data retention policy](policy-data-retention.md).

chunks.heading: Exit codes
chunks.text:
Exit codes

## Exit codes

| code | meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | success |
| 1 | error |
| 2 | refused: policy or precondition failed (wrong tier, missing reviewer) |
| 3 | refused: the cluster is frozen |

**2 and 3 are distinct on purpose.** A 2 means you asked for something you may
not have; a 3 means someone else is mid-incident and you should find out who
before forcing anything.

title: "Reference: deployment tiers"
tags: [reference, operations, platform]
---

chunks.heading: Reference: deployment tiers
chunks.text:
Reference: deployment tiers

# Reference: deployment tiers

Every Calder Group service belongs to exactly one tier. The tier decides
rollout order, soak period, review requirements and page policy. **A service
without a tier does not deploy** — the admission controller rejects it.

chunks.heading: The tiers
chunks.text:
The tiers

## The tiers

| tier | what is in it | rollout order | soak |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | revenue path: checkout, payments, cart, identity | last | 14 days |
| **2** | customer-visible but not revenue: search, recommendations, account | second | 7 days |
| **3** | internal: dashboards, batch, developer tooling | **first** | 48 hours |

**Rollout is always 3 → 2 → 1.** A platform change reaches the revenue path
only after it has survived everything else. This ordering is not negotiable and
there is no expedite path; a change urgent enough to skip tiers is an incident
response, which is a different procedure with a different approval.

chunks.heading: Soak periods
chunks.text:
Soak periods

## Soak periods

The soak is measured from the moment the **last** service in a tier finishes
rolling, not from when the first one starts.

Tier 1's soak was raised from 48 hours to 14 days after
[the checkout outage](postmortem-checkout-outage.md), and the change is
recorded in [ADR-0019](adr-0019-calder-gateway.md). The argument for the longer
period is that the failure in that incident was only visible under real
checkout traffic, which has a weekly shape — a 48-hour soak can miss an entire
class of weekend behaviour.

chunks.heading: Review requirements
chunks.text:
Review requirements

## Review requirements

| tier | reviewers | who can approve |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2, one from SRE | service owner + SRE on-call |
| 2 | 2 | service owner |
| 3 | 1 | anyone on the owning team |

chunks.heading: Page policy
chunks.text:
Page policy

## Page policy

- **Tier 1** pages 24/7. See [the on-call rota](guide-oncall-rota.md).
- **Tier 2** pages during business hours; out of hours it raises a ticket.
- **Tier 3** never pages. It files a ticket for the next working day.

**A tier 3 service that pages someone is a misconfiguration**, not a judgement
call. Fix the alert routing rather than absorbing the page.

chunks.heading: Changing a service's tier
chunks.text:
Changing a service's tier

## Changing a service's tier

A tier change is a pull request against `calder/service-registry`, reviewed by
the platform team. Moving *up* a tier (3 → 2, 2 → 1) takes effect at the next
rollout window. Moving *down* takes effect immediately, because reducing a
service's protections should never be blocked on scheduling.

chunks.heading: What tier does NOT decide
chunks.text:
What tier does NOT decide

## What tier does NOT decide

- **Resource quota.** That is the service's own budget.
- **Data classification.** See [the data retention policy](policy-data-retention.md);
  a tier 3 dashboard can hold tier-1-sensitive data and frequently does.

title: "Runbook: roll back a Calder Gateway release"

chunks.heading: Runbook: roll back a Calder Gateway release
chunks.text:
Runbook: roll back a Calder Gateway release

# Runbook: roll back a Calder Gateway release

> **This is the CURRENT rollback procedure**, for any tier that has migrated to
> Calder Gateway ([ADR-0019](adr-0019-calder-gateway.md)). If the tier is still
> on Helix Mesh, you want
> [the legacy mesh rollback](runbook-mesh-rollback-legacy.md) instead. **Check
> first.** The two procedures differ in step 3 and running the wrong one leaves
> the node in a state neither runbook describes.

**Severity:** used during an active incident. **Expected duration:** 8–12
minutes for one tier.

chunks.heading: When to use this
chunks.text:
When to use this

## When to use this

- Error rate above 2 % on any service behind the gateway, sustained 5 minutes.
- p99 latency above 400 ms on the checkout path.
- Any node reporting proxy config rejection.

Do **not** use this for a single unhealthy node. Drain that node instead; a
fleet rollback for one bad node is how a small problem becomes a large one.

chunks.heading: Which tier am I touching
chunks.text:
Which tier am I touching

## Which tier am I touching

```
calderctl gateway status --by-tier
```

The output names the release per tier. **A rollback is always scoped to one
tier**, per [the deployment tiers](reference-deployment-tiers.md). There is no
fleet-wide rollback command and its absence is deliberate.

chunks.heading: Procedure
chunks.text:
Procedure

## Procedure

**1. Announce.** Post in `#platform-incident` with the tier and the release you
are rolling back from. On-call lead acknowledges before you continue — see
[the on-call rota](guide-oncall-rota.md).

**2. Freeze the rollout.**

```
calderctl gateway freeze --tier <n>
```

This stops any in-flight progression. It does not revert anything.

**3. Revert the node proxy config, node by node.**

```
calderctl gateway rollback --tier <n> --to <previous-release> --max-surge 1
```

`--max-surge 1` is not optional. The node proxy serves every workload on its
node, so rolling more than one node at a time removes capacity from every
service simultaneously. This is the step that differs from the legacy
procedure, where the sidecar was per-pod and surge could safely be higher.

**4. Verify per node, not in aggregate.**

```
calderctl gateway verify --tier <n> --per-node
```

Aggregate health hides a single bad node behind 200 good ones. Check the
per-node table.

**5. Confirm the error rate has recovered** for a full 5 minutes before
unfreezing. A recovery that lasts 90 seconds is a coincidence.

**6. Unfreeze and write it up.**

```
calderctl gateway unfreeze --tier <n>
```

chunks.heading: If the rollback itself fails
chunks.text:
If the rollback itself fails

## If the rollback itself fails

Escalate immediately; do not retry. A failed rollback means the node proxy is
in a state the tooling does not model, and the second attempt tends to make the
state harder to describe rather than better. Page the platform networking lead
from [the on-call rota](guide-oncall-rota.md).

chunks.heading: Known gaps
chunks.text:
Known gaps

## Known gaps

- There is no dry-run mode. It has been requested twice.
- `--per-node` output is not paginated and is unreadable above ~400 nodes.

Runbook: roll back a Helix Mesh release (legacy)

# Runbook: roll back a Helix Mesh release (legacy)

> **LEGACY.** This applies only to tiers still running Helix Mesh
> ([ADR-0007](adr-0007-helix-mesh.md), superseded). Through 2026 that is most
> of tier 1. If the tier has migrated, you want
> [the gateway rollback](runbook-gateway-rollback.md) instead. **Check first.**
> The two procedures differ in step 3 and running the wrong one leaves the
> cluster in a state neither runbook describes.

**Severity:** used during an active incident. **Expected duration:** 10–15
minutes for one tier.

chunks.heading: When to use this
chunks.text:
When to use this

## When to use this

- Error rate above 2 % on any service in the mesh, sustained 5 minutes.
- p99 latency above 400 ms on the checkout path.
- Any pod reporting sidecar injection failure.

Do **not** use this for a single unhealthy pod. Restart that pod instead; a
fleet rollback for one bad pod is how a small problem becomes a large one.

chunks.heading: Which tier am I touching
chunks.text:
Which tier am I touching

## Which tier am I touching

```
calderctl mesh status --by-tier
```

The output names the release per tier. **A rollback is always scoped to one
tier**, per [the deployment tiers](reference-deployment-tiers.md). There is no
fleet-wide rollback command and its absence is deliberate.

chunks.heading: Procedure
chunks.text:
Procedure

## Procedure

**1. Announce.** Post in `#platform-incident` with the tier and the release you
are rolling back from. On-call lead acknowledges before you continue — see
[the on-call rota](guide-oncall-rota.md).

**2. Freeze the rollout.**

```
calderctl mesh freeze --tier <n>
```

This stops any in-flight progression. It does not revert anything.

**3. Revert the sidecar image and restart pods in waves.**

```
calderctl mesh rollback --tier <n> --to <previous-release> --max-surge 25%
```

`--max-surge 25%` is the tuned default. The sidecar is per-pod, so a quarter of
the fleet restarting concurrently costs a quarter of the capacity of the
services involved rather than all of it. This is the step that differs from the
gateway procedure, where the proxy is per-node and surge must be exactly 1.

**4. Verify per service, not in aggregate.**

```
calderctl mesh verify --tier <n> --per-service
```

Aggregate health hides one bad service behind 200 good ones. Check the
per-service table.

**5. Confirm the error rate has recovered** for a full 5 minutes before
unfreezing. A recovery that lasts 90 seconds is a coincidence.

**6. Unfreeze and write it up.**

```
calderctl mesh unfreeze --tier <n>
```

chunks.heading: If the rollback itself fails
chunks.text:
If the rollback itself fails

## If the rollback itself fails

Escalate immediately; do not retry. A failed rollback means sidecar state is
inconsistent across the tier, and the second attempt tends to widen the
inconsistency. Page the platform networking lead from
[the on-call rota](guide-oncall-rota.md).

chunks.heading: Known gaps
chunks.text:
Known gaps

## Known gaps

- There is no dry-run mode. It has been requested twice.
- Pods that fail injection during a rollback are silently skipped and must be
  found by hand afterwards. This is the known cause of the
  [checkout outage](postmortem-checkout-outage.md).
